picks.what: The Gymnasium and the Great Synagogue, postcard
picks.why: tinted view of the domed Great Synagogue (destroyed 1939), the town’s best-known landmark of the period

picks.what: General view with a new high-rise, postcard (Ruch)
picks.why: sharp general view over the center to the industrial horizon, 1930s high-rise at center; caption and borders trimmed

gaps: P0–P3: no candidates. P6: only flowerbed-dominated shots of the Chorzowska office towers (#7, #9), a street scene (#8) and a housing-estate aerial (#6); none shows the center well.
notes: #1’s printed caption sits in the sky above the synagogue and cannot be trimmed without cutting off the dome; drop #1 if captions are unacceptable. #2 (1934, its catalog note about a Matejko painting is a cataloging error; it is a photo) and #3/#5 (1936, St. Andrew’s Square) are good P5 alternatives.
